scenes.purpose: Open on the goal-to-workflow framing, attributed to MiniMax, and hold it long enough to read.
Show the real supplied MiniMax Code interface at the largest available size so product material is the hero, with a small persistent label.
Present the three confirmed product-described capabilities as single-line-per-card labels, attributed to MiniMax rather than measured results; headline only so no card text can overlap.
Hold the supplied CTA and URL to the final frame.

hook-headline.text: From one goal to a multi-step workflow

treatment.continuity: One white surface with ink type and MiniMax blue accents runs through every scene, so the title, the real screenshot and the cards read as one space. Each transition overlaps the outgoing scene by its transition length. The hook frames a goal; the product scene shows the real MiniMax Code window; the feature grid carries one short label per card plus a claim line; the end card closes on the supplied CTA. Every capability line is attributed to MiniMax and the grid header states that no measured results are shown.

holds.reason: Hook headline and attribution hold for reading before the crossfade.
Product scene settles on the real interface and holds.
Three single-label cards and the claim line stay legible after the stagger.
CTA and URL hold to the end.

treatment.hook: From one goal to a multi-step workflow, framed as how MiniMax describes MiniMax Code.
treatment.message: MiniMax Code, as MiniMax describes it: Coding and Work modes, agents that team up on tasks, and tools for images, video, audio, scripts and voiceovers. These are product claims, not measured results.
